correctness.rationale: For a simplicial involution, fixed points are exactly barycentric combinations constant on vertex orbits, producing an exact PL orbit-face complex. In the defined balanced bipartite generalized Mycielskian the admissible orbits are the apex and paired shore vertices strictly below the top level; compatibility is exactly absence of edges in the blown-up path. False-twin domination strongly collapses to an ordinary path. The path deletion-link suspension recursion yields the all-parameter 3-periodic classification. The full open-access Proposition 10 independently supplies the ambient homology degree and rank. Reduced Lefschetz on barycentric subdivision yields traces, rational coinvariant exactness yields quotient ranks. Boundary ell=0 and k=0 checked explicitly. The standalone executable checks invariant faces, GF2 homology and signed Lefschetz sums; finite verification is not used as proof.

value.rationale: A shore-exchange is the canonical nontrivial automorphism of the symmetric balanced-bipartite base graph, and fixed-point topology is a basic equivariant invariant of its growing generalized Mycielski independence complexes. The exact PL model, strong collapse and 3-periodic classification for all a and ell are structurally useful beyond a few finite Betti values, and explain the alternating involution character and quotient rational homology. Independence from the expanding shore size is a substantive boundary phenomenon, while the known ambient wedge ranks are not claimed as new.
